text: The paper reports pseudolabel correction on label 0 (err(f, y|S_0) < alpha_0), while for label 1 the bound exceeds alpha_1, because measured expansion is lower and the student's error on the weak labels higher, and, as the bound suggests, no correction occurs; the authors say their expansion-based theory can therefore differentiate cases where pseudolabel correction does and does not occur. For coverage expansion on label 1, T_1 expands to both S_1^good (c = 0.75) and S_1^bad (c = 0.55), and the worst-case err(f, y|T_1) over all training runs is 0.29, against a bound value of 0.33.
title: Measured expansion predicts pseudolabel correction and coverage expansion
